How to shoot it

Scene 1Closed comedones, before
Scene 2Glass clear skin, after
Scene 3Tap it on, ouch face
Keep this order. Talking points are examples, say it how you'd actually say it.
1Before: closed comedonesMust
  • Open on your closed comedones, up close. Forehead, chin or cheek, phone almost touching your skin, hard side light so every bump shows. No filter, no product.
  • Text on screen: your spicule hook (pick one below)
"if your chin looks like this, it's not acne. it's closed comedones"
2After: glass clear skinMust
  • Hard cut to the same spot, smooth and glowy. Same side light, same angle. Run a fingertip across it so we see how smooth it is.
  • Text: glass clear skin w/ spicule
"same spot now. no filter. glass skin"
3Tap it on + the ouch faceMust
  • Tap the spicule serum over the bumps. No rubbing. Bottle in the shot.
  • The ouch face is a must. When it tingles, squeeze your eyes, scrunch your face, go "ouch!" Make it big and real, like this clip. No ouch face, no pass.
  • Text: ouch.. that's the spicule working
"ouch.. ok it tingles. that's literally the spicules doing their thing""you tap it in, you don't rub it in. save this if your bumps never go away"

3

What's a spicule?

What it isTiny CICA spicules in a watery serum. Smaller than a grain of sand.
Why bumpsClosed comedones are dead skin and oil stuck right under the surface.The spicules exfoliate the top layer as you tap, so the bumps flatten out.
Why it tinglesThat little sting is the spicules working. That's your ouch moment.
4

Why it's the OG

Dupes copy one bottle. The original built five strengths.

Spicule serums started in Korea with this line, and 44.6M bottles later it's still the one everyone copies.Only the brand that made it first has the whole ladder, from a gentle 50 to an intensive 1300, so every skin has a place to start and a next step up.
